**Observations:**

- **Affected part**: Sugarcane leaf/leaf blade laid flat
- **Color pattern**: Distinct longitudinal bands of alternating green (central), yellow-orange (marginal), and pale cream/straw (outer edge, likely the sheath)
- **Texture**: No discrete spots, lesions, or necrotic patches — the discoloration runs the full length of the leaf parallel to the veins
- **Pattern type**: Classic "streaking" — narrow to broad stripes of chlorosis interleaved with green tissue, running parallel to the midrib and veins

**Reasoning through classes:**
- **Brown_Spot / Yellow_Spot**: Ruled out — no discrete circular/oval lesions
- **Grassy_Shoot / Sett_Rot**: Not applicable to a leaf symptom
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Typically involves leaf twisting, distortion, and chlorotic patches in the whorl — not a flat streaked leaf
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Causes midrib yellowing from the underside; here the midrib appears green while margins are yellow — opposite pattern
- **Leaf_Scald**: Produces thin pencil-line white/cream streaks; the stripes here are broader and more mosaic-like
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Causes irregular light/dark green mosaic patches, not pronounced yellow-orange longitudinal streaks
- **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: Sugarcane streak mosaic (SCSMV) produces characteristic longitudinal yellow-green streaks running parallel to leaf veins, often with orange/tan tones — this matches the image very well

The multiple-color longitudinal streaking (green center → yellow/orange transition → pale cream margins) running the entire leaf length is the hallmark of Sugarcane streak mosaic virus infection.
